articles.originalTitle: Candace Hill-Montgomery’s Spaces of Incompletion - ArtReview
articles.title: Candace Hill-Montgomery Exhibition in London Explores History and Resistance
articles.excerpt: A mini-survey exhibition of 21 works by artist Candace Hill-Montgomery spanning from 1971 to 2026 explores themes of racial inequality, power, and the pursuit of better futures.
articles.content: Staged at Hollybush Gardens in London, a mini-survey exhibition brings together 21 works by artist and poet Candace Hill-Montgomery, spanning weaves, paintings, photographs, a quilt, and a papier-mâché sculpture created between 1971 and 2026. The exhibition addresses subjects of racial inequality, power, and a yearning for better futures. Hill-Montgomery creates her woven works without pre-set coordinates or prior planning, incorporating found objects and various textiles. In the 2026 work 'Concept Doubles While Shorts on Circumstance Rumbles', wool and mohair spheres are combined, with the piece suspended from a Katanga Cross, a copper object historically used as currency in parts of the Democratic Republic of Congo. The 2024 work 'Some Are Liars' references a poem by Walter Scott, while the 2025 piece 'Pope L’T Raining Day' includes vintage toy-train tracks to reference the Underground Railroad and honors the artist Pope.L. The exhibition runs through 18 July.

articles.originalTitle: 12 uplifting design stories we discovered in Finland this month - wallpaper.com
articles.title: Helsinki Design Week Showcases Urban Innovation and Creative Growth in Finland
articles.excerpt: Helsinki Design Week highlighted innovative urban design projects, circular architecture, and collaborative creative strategies across the Finnish capital this September.
articles.content: Held in September, Helsinki Design Week brought together innovative design approaches aimed at enhancing urban habitats and everyday life. A strategic planning document commissioned by the City of Helsinki's Economic Development Division outlined nine key actions for growing the creative sectors alongside urban development. During the event, architect Pekka Airaxin launched Kainuu, a new company delivering turnkey summer houses constructed from cross-laminated timber sourced from managed forests within an 80 km radius. Kainuu has already delivered 10 houses, with 20 more in the pipeline. Additionally, Finnish architect and theorist Juhanni Pallasmaa donated his entire 10,000-strong book collection to Helsinki's Architecture & Design Museum in honor of his 90th birthday, with 10 percent of the collection currently on display at a temporary space. Hotel refurbishments and material-led experimental projects further highlighted the city's ongoing design engagement.

articles.originalTitle: International designers collaborate with creators from Japan at London's V&A - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Explores Japanese Traditions and Contemporary Design
articles.excerpt: London's Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting the Craft x Tech exhibition, showcasing collaborations between international designers and Japanese craft masters from the Tokai region. The initiative explores the intersection of traditional techniques and contemporary design.
articles.content:
London's Victoria and Albert Museum (V&A) is presenting the second edition of the Craft x Tech exhibition, highlighting collaborations between international designers and craft masters from Japan. Initiated by creative director Hideki Yoshimoto and curator Maria Cristina Didero, the project focuses on the Tokai region following its initial 2024 iteration in Tohoku. Didero states that the initiative prioritizes active communication and interaction between contemporary designers and traditional Japanese techniques over mere preservation.

The exhibition features works resulting from creators stepping out of their conventional disciplines. Canadian designer Philippe Malouin collaborated with an enamel master to incorporate decoration into his practice, while South African designer Atang Tshikare used the Japanese iga kumihimo silk braiding technique to create an anthropomorphic lamp. The experimental works are available as limited editions and remain on display at the V&A until 30 September.

articles.originalTitle: TfL reveals civil engineering behind £15.3M step-free upgrades at Surrey Quays and Northolt - New Civil Engineer
articles.title: Surrey Quays and Northolt Stations Achieve Step-Free Access in London
articles.excerpt: Transport for London has announced step-free access improvements at Surrey Quays and Northolt stations, detailing engineering works and funding.
articles.content: Two London railway stations, Surrey Quays and Northolt, have achieved step-free access to accommodate wheelchair users and passengers with pushchairs or luggage. According to Transport for London, the improvements at Surrey Quays were funded through an 80.8 million pound package. Lead designer AtkinsRéalis and contractor Morgan Sindall Infrastructure focused on reducing carbon impact by utilizing low-carbon CEM 3 concrete and electric arc furnace steel. The compound area used a direct power connection without generators alongside electric forklifts. Construction began in January 2023 and concluded in September 2026. Meanwhile, Northolt station on the West Ruislip branch received a new footbridge and lift to provide step-free access between the street and trains. The Northolt project cost an estimated 15.3 million pounds, with works starting in February 2025 and finishing by September 2026. Northolt marks the 95th station on the Tube network to offer step-free access.

articles.originalTitle: They’re Building Something New in Allentown, Leaving Venturi Scott Brown in Limbo - architecturalrecord.com
articles.title: Allentown Art Museum Plans New Facility as Venturi Scott Brown Addition Faces Uncertain Future
articles.excerpt: The Allentown Art Museum announced plans to relocate to a new downtown facility, leaving the future of its previous Venturi Scott Brown and Associates-designed addition uncertain.
articles.content: The Allentown Art Museum announced plans to relocate to a new facility designed by Studios Architecture in downtown Allentown, Pennsylvania. The 55,000-square-foot, $55 million museum is planned at the intersection of 10th and Hamilton Streets, with construction expected to begin in the summer of 2027 and completion anticipated by 2029. This relocation comes less than 15 years after the completion of the expansion designed by Venturi Scott Brown and Associates. Finished in 2012, the extension faced budget constraints during the economic downturn. Feasibility studies later determined that due to deferred maintenance and unresolved issues stemming from past budget cuts, constructing a purpose-built facility was the optimal path. Museum CEO Max Weintraub stated that the institution is in talks with commercial and public organizations regarding the purchase of the current facilities, noting that demolition has not been discussed, though the debossed facade signage will require modification.

articles.originalTitle: planted roof connects concrete casa cieno by TAC to oaxacan coast - designboom.com
articles.title: Casa Cieno on the Oaxacan Coast Features an Inward-Facing Design by TAC
articles.excerpt: Designed by TAC Taller Alberto Calleja in Puerto Escondido, Mexico, Casa Cieno integrates interior courtyards, a central pool, and a green roof to establish a relationship with its coastal surroundings.
articles.content: Located in Puerto Escondido along the coast of Oaxaca, Mexico, Casa Cieno was designed by the team at TAC Taller Alberto Calleja. Situated on a 1,500-square-meter plot in the El Vigía sector, the residence turns inward rather than facing the sea directly, utilizing vegetation and controlled openings to connect with its site. The main volume is rotated diagonally relative to the property boundaries, forming green patios that serve as a buffer. Organized around a central pool, the layout separates social and private zones while maintaining spatial continuity through courtyards. A circular roof opening frames the sky above the pool, introducing natural light to the interior. The material palette combines exposed concrete and wood chosen to respond to coastal climatic conditions and weather over time. Above, a green roof extends the living space while restoring site vegetation and offering views toward the sea and mountains.

The main volume of the residence is positioned diagonally in relation to the property boundaries, creating green buffer zones between the building and neighboring properties. The design team separated the social and private areas through the water element, with pathways crossing the pool to connect to two bedrooms. A circular opening in the roof slab frames the sky above the pool, introducing natural light into the interior. The material palette combines exposed concrete and wood, selected in response to the climatic conditions of the Oaxacan coast and intended to age with the site. A green roof extends the living space above, restoring part of the displaced vegetation while contributing to the residence's natural climate control.

articles.originalTitle: Between Burning Forests and Utopian Cities: Designing the Climate Transition - ArchDaily
articles.title: Designing the Climate Transition: Between Catastrophe Scenarios and Technological Utopias
articles.excerpt: While climate change discussions frequently focus on apocalyptic scenarios or technological salvation, the crucial, gradual work of multi-decade repair, adaptation, and maintenance remains largely underappreciated in design narratives.
articles.content: While cinematic and literary narratives frequently explore climate failure, technological transformations and smart cities offer optimized resource management and new urban futures. Projects such as The Line at NEOM propose entirely new urban conditions independent of existing physical constraints, offering a clean slate for future living. However, the climate transition will rely less on a single breakthrough and more on decades of parallel work streams involving adaptation, maintenance, repair, and resilience. Ordinary interventions—such as retrofitting buildings, gradually shifting energy systems, and restoring landscapes—constitute the cumulative foundation of systemic change. The primary challenge for designers and storytellers lies in visualizing and bringing this slow, distributed middle ground of transformation into the collective imaginary, moving beyond the binary of catastrophe and technological salvation.

articles.originalTitle: Black Wall Street Journey: Re and De Imagining Black Progress: Rick Lowe | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Rick Lowe's Largest Institutional Solo Exhibition Opens at the University of Michigan
articles.excerpt: Rick Lowe's largest institutional solo exhibition in the United States, Black Wall Street Journey, opens at the University of Michigan Museum of Art. The show combines art, data, and research to examine community prosperity.
articles.content: Marking Rick Lowe's largest institutional solo exhibition in the United States, Black Wall Street Journey opened at the University of Michigan Museum of Art. Running from September 26, 2026, to January 24, 2027, the exhibition brings together painting, sculpture, and public installation. The project is the culmination of the artist's three-year residency at the university's Institute for Social Research. Developed in collaboration with researchers, data scientists, and students, the work examines forces shaping wealth and opportunity across income, education, housing, and business ownership. In other developments, Adriana Varejão is preparing to represent Brazil at the 61st Biennale di Venezia with a presentation curated by Diane Lima, placing her in conversation with artist Rosana Paulino. Varejão's exhibition, titled Comigo ninguém pode, is installed within the Brazilian Pavilion's modernist structure.

articles.originalTitle: Glenn Brown in: Fail We May, Sail We Must | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Works from the Brown Collection on View in London
articles.excerpt: Curated by Glenn Brown and Edgar Laguinia, the exhibition brings together artworks spanning six centuries at the Brown Collection in London.
articles.content: Curated by Glenn Brown and his husband Edgar Laguinia, the exhibition titled Fail We May, Sail We Must is on view at the Brown Collection through August 7, 2027. The presentation features paintings, sculptures, drawings, prints, and ceramics by more than twenty artists spanning six centuries, incorporating spliced collages, double images, and elongated figures. The exhibition aims to challenge the mechanisms of the mind and create connections between works not typically seen together. Additionally, the Fall 2026 issue of Gagosian Quarterly has been published, coinciding with a catalogue raisonné and exhibition dedicated to Brice Marden. In other developments, Adriana Varejão opened her studio to share her working practice as she prepares new works to represent Brazil at the 61st Biennale di Venezia. Curated by Diane Lima, the Brazilian Pavilion features Varejão alongside Rosana Paulino, reflecting on colonial narratives and history.

articles.originalTitle: Switzerland’s Fondation Beyeler opens £109.7m expansion - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Basel's Fondation Beyeler Opens £109.7m Expansion Designed by Peter Zumthor
articles.excerpt: Basel's Fondation Beyeler has expanded with three new structures designed by Peter Zumthor and doubled its parkland. The museum is implementing a limited-capacity inauguration period through 14 January 2027 to optimize visitor processes.
articles.content:
The Fondation Beyeler in Basel, Switzerland, is opening its new expansion this weekend. Costing around SFr 120m (£109.7m), the project adds three new structures designed by Swiss architect Peter Zumthor and regenerates the museum grounds. The principal Wyss building, named after donor Hansjörg Wyss, increases exhibition space by 1,500 sq. m alongside the 1997 Renzo Piano building. The freestanding Ammann Pavilion serves as a venue for recitals and performances, while the Erlen Torhaus adds office space to an 18th-century villa on the property.

The surrounding parkland has doubled to nearly 20,000 sq. m, featuring new installations by artists such as Louise Bourgeois and Rachel Whiteread. An inaugural exhibition titled Constellations runs until 5 September 2027, displaying 150 works across both the original and new spaces. Zumthor constructed the Wyss building's exterior walls using rammed concrete with crushed limestone from the Jura Mountains. Rather than hosting a large celebration, the museum is running a restricted visitor period from 26 September to 14 January 2027 to optimize operations, according to director Sam Keller.

articles.originalTitle: Lisa Bradley Moves Beyond Luminosity at the Delaware Art Museum - hyperallergic.com
articles.title: Lisa Bradley's Abstract Paintings Open at the Delaware Art Museum
articles.excerpt: The Delaware Art Museum presents Beyond Luminosity, an exhibition bringing together the artist's most recent body of work for public view.
articles.content: The Delaware Art Museum presents Lisa Bradley: Beyond Luminosity, opening on September 19. Organized by DelArt Head Curator Margaret Winslow and Art Bridges Fellow Hilda Delgado, the exhibition offers audiences an engagement with Bradley's recent body of work, presented publicly for the first time. The presentation features 10 large-scale oil on canvas paintings and eight works on paper. Art historian Carter Ratcliff describes Bradley's abstractions as depicting a pause between vast energetic pulses. Informed by a strong interest in spiritual experiences, the artist achieves an expression of simultaneous movement and stillness within her luminous compositions. This exhibition builds upon the museum's longstanding connection to the artist, which includes the 2009 acquisition of her painting Akasa II. A complementary 120-page monograph featuring insights from curators, critics, and art historians accompanies the exhibition.

articles.originalTitle: Turner Prize 2026 opens in North Yorkshire at the Middlesbrough Institute of Modern Art - theartnewspaper.com
articles.title: Turner Prize 2026 Exhibition Opens at Middlesbrough Institute
articles.excerpt: The 2026 Turner Prize exhibition has opened to the public at the Middlesbrough Institute of Modern Art in northern England.
articles.content: The latest Turner Prize exhibition has opened to the public at the Middlesbrough Institute of Modern Art in northeast England. Shortlisted artists Tanoa Sasraku, Marguerite Humeau, Simeon Barclay, and Kira Freije are featured following their solo exhibitions from the past year. The selected artists engage with subjects such as ecological thought, human precarity, oil geopolitics, and the experience of deindustrialisation. Sasraku explores extractivism through immersive settings, while Humeau creates sculptural compositions from materials including beeswax and ancient wood. Barclay presents an architectural intervention exploring masculine identity and class, and Freije exhibits fragile figurative sculptures made from steel and aluminium. According to Tate Britain director Alex Farquharson, the works represent a cross-section of visual arts in Britain today. The winner will be announced on 10 December during a ceremony at the institute, receiving £25,000, while runners-up will be awarded £10,000 each.

articles.originalTitle: Why Toronto is fast becoming unmissable for art - artbasel.com
articles.title: Toronto Arts Scene Expands Amid Diversity and Infrastructure Growth
articles.excerpt: Toronto is gaining prominence in the art world through its immigrant population and hybrid cultural fabric. Biennials, new art trails, and independent spaces strengthen the city's infrastructure, while commercial and studio space needs shape ongoing developments.
articles.content: Kenneth Montague, founder of The Wedge Collection, notes that Toronto's hybrid identity and multicultural fabric form the foundation of Canadian art. With 51 percent of its population born abroad, the city hosts a dynamic scene featuring artists showcased at international platforms like the Venice Biennale. Running its fourth edition this current month, the Toronto Biennial centers on the shared geographies of the Great Lakes and Indigenous artists to foster global dialogue. Along the waterfront, the Lassonde Art Trail—backed by 25 million dollars in seed funding from Pierre Lassonde—features 17 new commissions winding through Biidaasige Park. While curators and directors highlight the civic impact of these urban revitalization projects, artists point out that commercial infrastructure remains critical for the ecosystem. Artist-run spaces and newly established downtown studio initiatives maintain a grassroots momentum, while institutions like the Art Gallery of Ontario and MOCA expand their programming and gallery footprints. Local participants observe that while Toronto's collector base holds significant potential, the demand for affordable studio spaces and institutional growth continues as the local arts community navigates rapid urban development.

articles.originalTitle: La vida secreta de las plantas: Anselm Kiefer en la Colección Grothe | Museum Exhibitions | News - Gagosian
articles.title: Anselm Kiefer Brings The Secret Life of Plants Exhibition to Barcelona
articles.excerpt: Fundació Catalunya La Pedrera–Casa Milà in Barcelona is hosting the first Anselm Kiefer exhibition in the city, bringing together around forty works from the collection of Hans Grothe.
articles.content: Fundació Catalunya La Pedrera–Casa Milà in Barcelona is hosting an exhibition titled The Secret Life of Plants. Scheduled from October 2, 2026, to January 24, 2027, the presentation gathers approximately forty works by Anselm Kiefer from the collection of Hans Grothe, alongside pieces from other private collections. The selection offers insight into the symbolic richness and material complexity of the artist's practice. At the core of the presentation is Opus Magnum, a series of vitrines on display for the first time in Spain. Conceived as archives of memory, these works assemble books, plants, stones, and fabrics in a dialogue between history, myth, science, and spirituality. In parallel, the Fall 2026 issue of Gagosian Quarterly has been released, featuring various contributions and previews of upcoming projects. Meanwhile, Adriana Varejão prepared new works destined to represent Brazil at the 61st Biennale di Venezia. Curated by Diane Lima, the Brazilian Pavilion places Varejão in conversation with Rosana Paulino to reflect on colonial wounds and the rewriting of history in Brazil.

articles.originalTitle: Major Retrospective of Sri Lankan Architect Geoffrey Bawa Opens at the Vitra Design Museum - architecturalrecord.com
articles.title: Major Geoffrey Bawa Retrospective Opens at the Vitra Design Museum
articles.excerpt: Examining the five-decade career of influential 20th-century architect Geoffrey Bawa, a major retrospective has opened at the Vitra Design Museum in Germany. Featuring over 250 drawings, models, and archival documents, the exhibition runs through February 28, 2027.
articles.content: Highlighting the career of Geoffrey Bawa, recognized as one of the most influential architects of the 20th century, a comprehensive retrospective exhibition has opened at the Vitra Design Museum in Weil am Rhein, Germany. Marking the first major exhibition dedicated to Bawa in over twenty years, the showcase presents more than 250 drawings, models, photographs, furniture pieces, and archival documents spanning five decades of his professional practice. Organized by the Vitra Design Museum, M+, and the Wüstenrot Foundation in collaboration with the Geoffrey Bawa Trust, the retrospective encompasses diverse projects ranging from the Bentota Beach Hotel to the Kandalama Hotel. Newly commissioned photographs by Iwan Baan emphasize the lived-in character of the buildings and their integration with surrounding landscapes. The exhibition closely examines the architect's spatial relationship with terrain and highlights his collaborations with local craftspeople and artists. Lebanese architect Lina Ghotmeh designed the scenography to evoke the sensory qualities inherent in Bawa's built works. Following its presentation in Germany, the exhibition is scheduled to travel to M+ in Hong Kong in June 2027. The retrospective remains on view at the Vitra Design Museum through February 28, 2027.

articles.originalTitle: About the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires Exhibition Opens at the V&A
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum explores 1,600 years of artistic production across two empires in a major upcoming exhibition.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum invites visitors to explore 1,600 years of artistic production with the exhibition 'Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires', opening on 7 November 2026. Spanning from AD 330 to 1922, the exhibition brings together over 200 objects to examine the distinct yet connected traditions of the Byzantine and Ottoman empires. Hosted at V&A South Kensington, the showcase highlights the creative legacy of an imperial capital that shaped the Mediterranean world and beyond. The exhibition features four main sections: Grand Beginnings, Heaven and Earth, Power and Reach, and Life in the City. Across these sections, visitors can view rarely seen decorative arts, including fine silks, historic garments, ceramic tiles, mosaics, precious metalwork, jewellery, sculptures, architectural furnishings, manuscripts, and paintings. The curation traces changes in patronage, imperial spectacle, religious coexistence, and urban life, concluding with the influence of Byzantine and Ottoman art on 19th-century Europe.

articles.originalTitle: Standout Collectible Designs at Paris Design Week 2026 - WWD
articles.title: Standout Collections and Contemporary Designs Unveiled at Paris Design Week
articles.excerpt: The 16th edition of Paris Design Week showcased collections blending traditional craftsmanship, natural forms, and contemporary design.
articles.content: The 16th edition of Paris Design Week featured participation from 500 exhibitors across showrooms in Saint-Germain-des-Prés and other locations, highlighting creations rooted in traditional techniques and natural forms. Draga & Aurel showcased their Crisalide side tables at Galerie BSL, combining colored glass, blown-glass legs, and brass bases. Design firm Pinto and Nobilis revived their collaboration with the Foundation fabric and wall-covering collection. Yves Salomon Éditions unveiled Tactile Monuments, its first complete interior collection centered on merino shearling and natural volumes. Swedish design house Veermakers opened its first Paris showroom in Le Marais to highlight Scandinavian cabinetmaking traditions. Nordic Knots presented hand-knotted wool rugs inspired by Swedish Grace. Modern Metier partnered with Rudy Guénaire to present Tropic of Capricorn, while Garnier & Linker introduced Aurora, an outdoor lighting collection in cast aluminum and alabaster. Franck Genser exhibited his Piscine VI collection, and Hervet Manufacturier presented its full range of living and working furniture drawing on six generations of woodworking expertise.

articles.originalTitle: Sansetsukon x Es Devlin: MILK - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Sansetsukon and Es Devlin to Present Live Performance at V&A East Storehouse
articles.excerpt: Dance collective Sansetsukon will present MILK, a live performance responding to Es Devlin’s installation The Everythingists, for free at the V&A East Storehouse on 3 October 2026.
articles.content: Dance collective Sansetsukon is preparing to stage MILK, a new live performance responding to Es Devlin’s installation The Everythingists. The event will take place on 3 October 2026 at Gallery 2 within the V&A East Storehouse. Scheduled for 2:00 PM, 5:00 PM, and 8:00 PM, each performance lasts between 25 and 30 minutes and is free to the public. Through dance, sound, light, and shadow, the performance creates a dialogue between the dancers, the installation, and the surrounding gallery space. The work draws inspiration from Rayonism and concepts regarding humans empowered by machines and machines empowered by artists. Performers move through the gallery to a soundscape created by reworking audio elements from The Everythingists. The ensemble features dancers Joshua Shanny-Wynter, Deavion Brown, Robbie Ordoña, Peter Butler, Tania Dimbelolo, Lois Samphier, and Anna Watanabe, with a musical composition by Serian Griffiths and sound design by Nana Nakashima.

articles.originalTitle: 200,000 young people and counting: Tate celebrates a new generation with landmark commission for young artists - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Collective Reaches 200,000 Members and Launches Landmark Open Call
articles.excerpt: Tate Collective, the free membership scheme for 16 to 25-year-olds, has reached 200,000 members and launched an open call for a new artwork to be displayed at Tate Modern.
articles.content: Tate Collective, a free membership scheme for 16 to 25-year-olds, has reached a milestone of 200,000 members. To mark the occasion, an open call has been launched inviting members to create a new artwork for display at Tate Modern alongside figures such as Andy Warhol, Salvador Dalí, and Marina Abramović. The winning commission will be selected by a jury chaired by Rosalie Doubal and will go on display in March 2027, with submissions closing on 19 October. Concurrently, Tate Modern Lates is celebrating its 10th anniversary, having drawn 870,000 attendees over the past decade to after-hours events featuring live music, performances, and workshops. Karin Hindsbo, Interim Director of Tate, stated that the members represent a generation choosing to engage with art and ideas. The anniversary celebrations will culminate on 30 October with a special Late event programmed by Shygirl. Tate Collective membership offers various discounts and access to creative opportunities with support from patrons and foundations.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale College Architettura 2026/2027: the 12 selected projects - labiennale.org
articles.title: Twelve Projects Selected for Biennale College Architettura 2026-2027
articles.excerpt: Twelve projects have been selected for the third edition of Biennale College Architettura. The projects by practitioners under 30 will be developed during a workshop from 22 to 30 September 2026.
articles.content: Twelve projects have been selected for the 3rd edition of Biennale College Architettura 2026–2027. The emerging practitioners under 30 originate from China, Croatia, Italy, Mexico, Syria, Spain, Turkey, Tunisia, the USA, and Hungary. The initiative complements the 20th International Architecture Exhibition, titled Do Architecture and curated by Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu, serving as a research, experimentation, and production laboratory. The open call attracted over 80 emerging practitioners from 36 countries. The 12 selected projects are presented by Ahlem Balghouthi, Fabio Bari, Stav Bouzaglo, Antonino Caridi, Yiying Chen, Alejandro Ferrer Esplugues, Jin Gao, Nisa Gökgöz, Matej Orkić, Julia Polefko, Ahmad Salah, and Guillermo Sanchez Cardenas. The workshop will take place from 22 to 30 September 2026, coordinated by Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu alongside tutors. Following the workshop, up to four projects will be selected to receive a 25,000 euro grant for the realization of the final work, which will be presented out of competition during Biennale Architettura 2027.

articles.originalTitle: ARTIST ROOMS: Robert Rauschenberg at Tate Modern, 21 September 2026 - December 2027 – Press Release - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Modern Opens Large-Scale Robert Rauschenberg Display
articles.excerpt: Tate Modern is launching a large-scale free display of over 20 works by Robert Rauschenberg spanning three decades to mark the centenary of his birth.
articles.content: Tate Modern is launching a large-scale free display of works by Robert Rauschenberg, running from 21 September 2026 to December 2027. Marking the centenary of the artist's birth, the presentation brings together over 20 works spanning three decades, including paintings, prints, and kinetic installations. At the heart of the presentation are Glut sculptures, including three newly gifted by the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation to the Tate Americas Foundation. Curated by Gregor Muir, Andrew de Brún, and Julia Blaut, the display foregrounds Rauschenberg's engagement with dance and performance, featuring metal sculptures, performance sets, and costume designs. The exhibition is organized as part of the ARTIST ROOMS touring programme, jointly managed by Tate and the National Galleries of Scotland.

articles.originalTitle: Maison Michel Celebrates 90 Years of Hatmaking With New Exhibition at Chanel’s Le19M - WWD
articles.title: Parisian Hatmaker Maison Michel Celebrates 90th Anniversary With Le19M Exhibition
articles.excerpt: Parisian hatmaker Maison Michel is marking its 90th anniversary with an exhibition at La Galerie du 19M, highlighting traditional craftsmanship techniques and historical archives.
articles.content: Renowned Parisian hatmaker Maison Michel is celebrating its 90th anniversary with an exhibition that highlights its extensive craftsmanship heritage. Opening on Sept. 23 at La Galerie du 19M, the craft hub in northern Paris, the exhibition titled “Metamorphoses — The Hats of Maison Michel” runs until Dec. 13. Part of Chanel’s network of specialized workshops since 1997, the house focuses as much on ancient tools and techniques as it does on final designs. Curated by artistic director Priscilla Royer and Palais Galliera museum director Emilie Hammen, the display begins with tree trunks carved into raw hat shapes and a selection of the 4,000 wooden hat blocks held in its archives. Visitors can view specially commissioned artworks, alongside sections dedicated to modistes working with canvas, organza, leather, and tweed. The exhibition also features a replica of an early 20th-century milliner's shop where weekly filmmaking workshops will be hosted. The curators note that headgear has evolved from a social signifier governed by strict past conventions into a modern form of personal self-expression.

articles.originalTitle: EXCLUSIVE: Jacquemus Filled His New Miami Design District Flagship With Art — and Fine Design - WWD
articles.title: Jacquemus Opens New Flagship Boutique in Miami Design District
articles.excerpt: Paris-based fashion house Jacquemus is opening a two-story flagship boutique in the Miami Design District. Conceived by the founder, the 2,900-square-foot space incorporates blue-chip artworks, antiques, and bespoke design pieces.
articles.content: Paris-based fashion house Jacquemus is launching a 2,900-square-foot flagship boutique in Miami's Design District, spanning two floors. Conceived by founder Simon Porte Jacquemus in collaboration with architectural firm Oma, the interior echoes elements from earlier boutiques in Paris and Courchevel. The space integrates artworks by Germaine Richier, Aristide Maillol, Joan Miró, and Pablo Picasso, alongside furnishings by Frank Lloyd Wright and Jean Royère. Chief executive officer Sarah Benady described Miami as a natural convergence point for fashion, art, and design between the United States and Latin America. The boutique includes a dedicated shoe salon, a private VIC sunroom, and infrastructure prepared for an upcoming beauty line through a partnership with L'Oréal. Additionally, the location will offer an exclusive powder and mint blue edition of the Nike Moon Shoe. This opening follows recent retail expansions in New York and Los Angeles as part of the brand's targeted international retail strategy.
